## Introduction

_tblocks_ is a Tcl application and Tcl package which can be used to translate
simple Markdown files into SVG graphics.

Here the typical Hello World example with Markdown code 
which be automatically converted to a SVG graphics using a command line like
`tblocks hello.md hello.svg`: 

```{.shell label=hello1 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=600}
## Hello

- entry 1
- entry 2
- entry 3

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## World!

- entry 4
- entry 5
- entry 6

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.
```

You can see the default color coding and the default diagram style which is
blocks. By using a YAML header you can changing these defaults.

## Styling the Diagram

There are two ways to change the diagram type, the font and the colors for the
output. Either you provide the application the appropriate command line
option, or you give these settings within a YAML header section at the
beginning of the Markdown file.

### Styling Colors

Here is a modified version where we set the colors for the first diagram to magentish:

```{.shell label=hello2 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=600}
---
color1: "#DDDDFF" "#BBBBEE" "#404090"
---
## Hello

- entry 1
- entry 2
- entry 3

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## World!

- entry 4
- entry 5
- entry 6

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.
```

The default colors are based on the standard order of ANSI colors, so we have
black, which is used for the text, then pastel version of red, green, yellow,
blue, magenta and cyan. Here you see an extension of the first plot. For space issues I hide most of the Markdown code here:

```
## Hello Red

- entry 1
- entry 2
- entry 3

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## Hello Green

- entry 4
...
```



```{.shell label=hello3 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=900 echo=FALSE}
## Hello Red

- entry 1
- entry 2
- entry 3

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## Hello Green

- entry 4
- entry 5
- entry 6

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## Hello Yellow

- entry 7
- entry 8
- entry 9

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## Hello BLue

- entry 10
- entry 11
- entry 12

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## Hello Magenta

- entry 13
- entry 14
- entry 15

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.

## Hello Cyan

- entry 16
- entry 17
- entry 18

There can be as well some more text
in the lines below of the list.
```

## Diagram Types

The `mode` entry in the YAML header selects a diagram layout. The following
examples show layouts which are useful beyond the default block diagram.

### Sequence

The `sequence` layout presents a row of steps and can place a small icon in a
heading:

```{.shell label=sequence1 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=900}
---
mode: sequence
---

## Prepare

- Collect the input
- Validate the data

## Process icon:yes

- Apply the calculation
- Store the result

## Finish

- Review the output
- Report success
```

### Table

The `table` layout places two or more titled columns next to each other. Each
item should be a Markdown list entry:

```{.shell label=table1 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=900}
---
mode: table
---

## DO icon:yes

- Use references for read-only parameters.
- Keep class variables private.
- Prefer standard-library containers.

## DON'T icon:no

- Pass large objects by value.
- Use C strings when std::string is available.
- Leave data members public in a class.
```

### Input and Output

The `inout` layout is intended for an input, a processing function, and an
output:

```{.shell label=inout1 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=700}
---
mode: inout
---

## KNOWN

Input

The data available
at the start.

## UNKNOWN

Function

The transformation
to be developed.

## KNOWN

Output

The expected result
after processing.
```

### Timeline

The `timeline` layout distributes dated or ordered events along a horizontal
timeline:

```{.shell label=timeline1 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=900}
---
mode: timeline
---

## 1. Planning

2024 - Requirements
2025 - First prototype

## 2. Development

2025 - Implementation
2026 - Integration

## 3. Release

2026 - Documentation
2026 - Public release
```

### Comparison

The `compare` layout uses `###` subheadings for labeled parts of each item:

```{.shell label=compare1 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=900}
---
mode: compare
---

## Inheritance (Is-A)

### Definition

Class B is a subtype of class A.

### Implementation

Reuse and specialize inherited behavior.

## Composition (Has-A)

### Definition

Class B contains or delegates to class A.

### Implementation

Combine independent components.
```

### Circular

The `circular` layout uses one top-level `#` heading for the central circle
and one or more `##` headings for surrounding subsections. Three, four, and
five subsections use compact fixed layouts; additional subsections are placed
around the circle:

```{.shell label=circular1 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=900}
---
mode: circular
---

# 1. Core Topic :: With Two Lines

## 1.1 First Area
The first subsection is centered below
its heading.

## 1.2 Second Area
The next subsection is placed clockwise.

## 1.3 Third Area
The remaining subsections follow around
the central circle.
```

A second circular diagram can use a pastel palette by overriding `color1`
with text, fill, and border colors:

```{.shell label=circular2 cmd="tclsh ../tblocks/tblocks.tcl %i %b.svg" chunk.ext=md ext=svg fig.width=900}
---
mode: circular
color1: "#17452d" "#ddf5df" "#86c99a"
---

# 1. Sustainable :: Development

## 1.1 Social
Support fair access and inclusive participation.

## 1.2 Economic
Build durable value and resilient processes.

## 1.3 Environmental
Reduce waste and preserve natural resources.
```
